page: Amazon Web Services c8id.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture, featuring an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz. The virtual instance provides 16 vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core on the x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 system memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is addressed locally through a bundled 950 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, complemented by an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile. No discrete GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark results show competitive single-threaded capabilities. Geekbench single-core performance scores 2219.0, placing it in the top 10 percent, supported by top-tier text processing (2967.0) and high single-threaded throughput in compression workloads like gzip (34.49 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.44 GB/sec). Small language model text generation achieves 390.86 tokens per second, also ranking in the top 10 percent, leveraging Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets. Multi-core execution, PassMark metrics, and memory bandwidth largely place in the middle 50 percent, reflecting balanced parallel compute within its 16-vCPU envelope.

The bundled NVMe storage and DDR5 memory speed deliver strong qualitative efficiency for compute-heavy workloads needing low-latency scratch disk access without auxiliary storage attachment costs. With its compute-oriented memory ratio and rapid instruction execution, the instance is appropriate for batch data processing, single-thread-limited compilation tasks, lightweight CPU-based model inference, and web serving architectures requiring high local I/O performance.
